item.title: #3592101: Make React Code Components portable across Drupal and headless frontends
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592101 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

React Code Components (the small React components authors write for Canvas) previously had to use Drupal-specific APIs to read page metadata, site branding, and content, which meant they could not be reused as-is in a headless frontend. This change makes the same component code work unmodified in both Drupal-rendered pages and React-based headless applications (Next.js, TanStack Start, Astro). Existing components keep working in Drupal and in Canvas Workbench previews without any changes; the canvas pull CLI command can also automatically rewrite eligible components to the new APIs when the connected site and installed package support it. Headless applications also gain a same-origin JSON:API proxy so browser-side requests (including draft/preview reads) can reach Drupal safely without exposing credentials.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: getPageData(), getSiteData(), new JsonApiClient(), Region, and RegionsProvider are deprecated; they keep working in Drupal-rendered Code Components and Workbench but throw actionable migration errors in headless React apps.
  • New API: New drupal-canvas/react exports usePageContext(), useSiteContext(), CanvasContextProvider, useJsonApiClient(), and JsonApiClientProvider give React Code Components a single, framework-portable way to read page/site data and make JSON:API requests.

Technical details

The core addition is a shared CanvasContext ({ page, site }) carried by a new CanvasContextProvider (packages/drupal-canvas/src/context.tsx) and read with usePageContext()/useSiteContext(). Rendering integrations, the Drupal island renderer, the headless CanvasComponentTree, and both Workbench preview paths, mount the provider automatically; a missing provider or missing page/site value makes the hooks return null and emit a deduplicated warnOnce() warning rather than fetching data or defaulting. Headless SDK's fetchPage() now returns this context alongside the component tree as page.context.

JSON:API access is consolidated the same way: useJsonApiClient()/JsonApiClientProvider (packages/drupal-canvas/src/jsonapi-client-context.tsx) expose a shared JsonApiClient built on @drupal-api-client/json-api-client (createJsonApiClient() in jsonapi-client.ts), replacing separate client implementations previously used by the drupal-canvas package and the headless SDK's draft client. Browser requests in headless apps go through a new same-origin proxy (packages/headless/src/server/jsonapi-proxy.ts, and jsonapi-proxy.ts/jsonapi-proxy.test.ts in drupal-canvas) that authenticates from the draft-preview session cookie, restricts requests to the configured backend and endpoint set, and keeps authenticated responses out of shared caches.

Legacy API compatibility is enforced with an explicit runtime marker rather than environment sniffing: declareCanvasRuntime()/getCanvasRuntime() (packages/drupal-canvas/src/runtime.ts) is set by Drupal and Workbench integrations, and assertLegacyRuntime() (migration.ts) throws an actionable error, including an AI-agent migration prompt, when getPageData(), getSiteData(), or new JsonApiClient() is invoked outside those two environments. On the PHP side, CanvasContentContextBuilder and changes to CodeComponentDataProvider and SiteDataController supply this context data and advertise capabilities.contextHooks from /canvas/api/v0/site-data, which the CLI's pull codemod (packages/cli/src/utils/getter-codemod.ts, context-hook-support.ts) checks before rewriting a component's safe, unconditional getPageData()/getSiteData() calls to the new hooks. Region and RegionsProvider are deprecated in favor of the page-variants model from ADR 19.

Upgrade

No action is required to keep existing Code Components working in Drupal or Workbench. To make a component portable to headless frontends, migrate off the deprecated APIs:

// Before
import { getPageData, getSiteData } from 'drupal-canvas';

// After
import { usePageContext, useSiteContext } from 'drupal-canvas/react';

export default function PageHeader() {
  const page = usePageContext();
  const site = useSiteContext();
  if (!page || !site) return null;
  return (
    <header>
      <a href={site.branding.homeUrl}>{site.branding.siteName}</a>
      <h1>{page.pageTitle}</h1>
    </header>
  );
}

Replace direct client construction the same way:

// Before
const client = new JsonApiClient({ baseUrl });

// After
import { useJsonApiClient } from 'drupal-canvas/react';
const client = useJsonApiClient();

Running canvas pull against a site that advertises capabilities.contextHooks (and with drupal-canvas/react installed) converts eligible files automatically and reports any calls it could not safely convert.

item.title: #3592128: Remove experimental Canvas Headless properties and CLI flag
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592128 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

The Canvas Headless submodule has graduated out of experimental status. It is no longer marked hidden or experimental, so it now shows up and can be enabled like any other module instead of being concealed from the module list. Its description was also updated to reflect that it connects a headless frontend app to Canvas for editing and preview. Separately, the @drupal-canvas/create scaffolding CLI no longer requires the --experimental-headless flag: all headless frontend templates (Next.js, Astro, Nuxt, TanStack Start, Angular) are now offered directly in the interactive template picker, and non-interactive runs that omit --template fall back to the default template instead of erroring out.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: The canvas_headless submodule is no longer hidden/experimental, so it appears in the module list and can be enabled directly.
  • API change: The @drupal-canvas/create CLI's --experimental-headless flag and the experimental/experimentalHeadless options on its Template and CreateOptions types were removed.

Technical details

In modules/canvas_headless/canvas_headless.info.yml, the lifecycle: experimental and hidden: true keys were removed and the module description was rewritten. In the @drupal-canvas/create package, the experimental flag on each Template (in templates.json and the Template type) was dropped, along with the experimentalHeadless option on CreateOptions and the --experimental-headless Commander option. The template selection logic in the CLI's main command was simplified to always build its list from predefinedTemplates rather than filtering by an experimental flag; the special-case branch that auto-selected a single available template, or exited with an error in non-interactive mode when none was specified, was replaced with a straightforward fallback to the default template for non-interactive runs.

Upgrade

Remove any use of the --experimental-headless flag from scripts or documentation that invoke the CLI:

# before
npx @drupal-canvas/create@latest --experimental-headless

# after
npx @drupal-canvas/create@latest

The Canvas Headless module can now be enabled directly (it is no longer hidden), so no special discovery step is needed to find it in the module list.

item.title: #3592097: Include language alternates in Headless content API
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592097 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

Headless frontends built on Canvas can now get everything needed for a language switcher directly from the content API response, instead of having to derive it themselves. Each fetchPage() response's route object now lists every enabled language with its localized name, native name, a URL, whether that translation actually exists and is viewable, and whether it is the one currently being served. This mirrors the translation data already exposed to Code Components via getPageData(), so both APIs behave consistently.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: route in the Headless content API response now includes negotiatedLanguage and a translations list (langcode, name, nativeName, url, translationAvailable, current, external) for every enabled language.

Technical details

The new Drupal\canvas_headless\CanvasContentTranslationLinks service builds this data in CanvasContentController, and delegates the actual per-language enumeration to a new shared helper, Drupal\canvas\EntityTranslationMetadata::build(). That helper was extracted from the existing logic in CodeComponentDataProvider (which now calls it too), so Code Components and the headless API share one source of truth for langcode, name, nativeName, translationAvailable, and current. translationAvailable reflects both existence and view access; a denied or missing translation reports false and falls back to the entity's own URL in that language.

For the headless case, URL generation is more involved than the Code Component fallback: CanvasContentTranslationLinks::switchLinks() walks enabled language negotiation methods in configured order (following LanguageNegotiationUI delegation to the interface-language session negotiator), builds each link via the module's LanguageSwitcherInterface plugins, and strips out Canvas's editor-preview query parameters while forcing the session query parameter when session negotiation is active, so a translation link is unambiguous regardless of prior session state. Generated absolute URLs are then normalized by the new Drupal\canvas_headless\CanvasContentUrl::normalize(), which strips the scheme, host, and Drupal base path from same-site URLs (an external one is left absolute and flagged with external: true) so frontends can safely feed the result back into fetchPage(). The near-identical logic previously duplicated in CanvasContentResponseSubscriber for redirect targets was consolidated into this same helper.

The OpenAPI schema (RouteTranslation) and the SDK's TypeScript types (DrupalRouteTranslation, DrupalRoute in packages/headless/src/page.ts) were updated to document the new required negotiatedLanguage and translations fields, and docs/multilingual-sites-with-canvas-headless.md explains the filtering and public-URL-mapping pattern for consumers building a switcher.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">No breaking changes to existing fields. Frontends consuming fetchPage() and using the SDK's TypeScript types should update to a version that includes negotiatedLanguage and translations on DrupalRoute, since these are now required properties of the response schema. To build a switcher of only viewable translations:

const page = await fetchPage("/fr/page/1");
if (page && !("redirect" in page)) {
  const languageLinks = page.route.translations
    .filter((translation) => translation.translationAvailable)
    .map((translation) => ({
      label: translation.nativeName,
      active: translation.current,
      href: toPublicUrl(translation.langcode, translation.url),
    }));
}

Entries with external: true are absolute URLs (e.g. from domain-based language negotiation) and are not valid fetchPage() input; map them to a public URL instead of passing them back in.</parameter> <parameter name="collaboration">

Contribution

  • Opened: September 18, 2026

item.title: #3592115: Add Angular support to the Headless SDK and templates
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592115 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

Drupal Canvas's headless frontend tooling now supports Angular. A new @drupal-canvas/headless-angular adapter package and an experimental Angular starter template join the existing Next.js, Astro, Nuxt and TanStack Start integrations offered through Canvas Create. Developers can now build headless Angular 21 or 22 apps that render Canvas's component trees with server-side rendering and hydration, named slots, component discovery, and full support for Canvas's draft preview and publishing workflow. The starter defaults to Angular 22 and documents Angular 21 setup; Angular Workbench integration is explicitly out of scope for now.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New @drupal-canvas/headless-angular package providing Angular 21/22 bindings (component-tree rendering, SSR/hydration, draft-preview server endpoints, and a canvas-angular codegen tool) for building headless Canvas frontends, plus a new experimental angular starter template in Canvas Create.

Technical details

The new @drupal-canvas/headless-angular package mirrors the structure of the other framework adapters and builds on the shared, framework-agnostic @drupal-canvas/headless core (its client, server, components-endpoint, and component-registry submodules). It exposes:

  • Rendering primitives (CanvasComponentTree, CanvasElement, CanvasSlot, CanvasChildren, CanvasMarkerDirective, CanvasMarkup) built on Angular signals and NgComponentOutlet, which walk the component tree, resolve named slots against a CanvasComponentRegistry, and emit the data-canvas-* marker templates used by the visual editor.
  • An application layer (CanvasPageStore, canvasPageResolver, CanvasDraftSession, CanvasDocumentHead, provideCanvas()) that wires page data into Angular's router (via a resolver and TransferState for hydration), manages the draft-session/renewal state machine, and syncs <head> metadata.
  • A server layer (createCanvasHandler, createCanvasRequest in @drupal-canvas/headless-angular/server) implementing the same REST-style endpoints as the other adapters (/api/draft, /api/draft/renew, /api/disable-draft, /api/canvas/components, /api/canvas/page, /api/canvas/entity), enforcing private/no-store caching, CSP frame-ancestors merging for embedded previews, and an explicit allowlist (CanvasSession) so tokens and PKCE verifiers never cross into the browser-visible TransferState.
  • A canvas-angular CLI/tooling script that generates a browser-safe component registry module and a server-only metadata manifest module, meant to run before ng serve/ng build, analogous to the codegen used by the other adapters.

The package targets Angular's partial compilation output (verified by a build test asserting ɵɵngDeclareComponent rather than ɵɵdefineComponent in the built bundle) so it can be consumed by both Angular 21 (TypeScript 5.9) and Angular 22 (TypeScript 6) host apps via matching peer dependency ranges.

On the tooling side, templates.json in canvas-headless-templates gains an angular entry (marked experimental, sourced from a separate drupal-canvas/headless-templates GitHub repo), and Canvas Create's SetupSection framework picker now lists Angular alongside the four existing frameworks.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

Contribution

item.title: #3592030: Canvas AI: Remove obsolete region-based AI instructions and the unused page variant descriptions form
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592030 · 1 contributor · 56 comments

Summary

Canvas moved from theme-global regions (header, footer, sidebar, etc.) to page variants, where everything besides a page's main content is built as its own component tree in the Canvas editor. The Canvas AI module still had leftover instructions and an admin settings page from the old multi-region model, describing a capability that no longer exists. This change removes them: the AI page builder and template builder agents no longer reference regions other than content, and the "Page Variant Descriptions" admin settings page (where an admin could describe how AI should treat each page variant) is deleted since nothing read those descriptions anymore. Site owners who had configured page variant descriptions for AI will find that settings page and its data gone; AI-generated pages and templates will only ever place components in the content region, with header, navigation, footer or sidebar sections generated inside that same region only when explicitly requested in the prompt.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: The canvas_ai.page_variant.settings config object and its admin form at /admin/config/ai/canvas-ai-page-variant-settings ("Page Variant Descriptions") are removed; update hooks delete any existing config and rebuild routes.

Technical details

The [canvas_ai:available_regions] token is deleted from CanvasAiHooks::canvas_ai_token_info()/canvas_ai_tokens(), along with CanvasAiPageBuilderHelper::getAvailableRegions() and its helpers resolveVariantForContext()/getVariantDescription(), which used to resolve a page variant via PageVariantResolver and pull a per-variant AI description out of canvas_ai.page_variant.settings. Both CanvasBuilder and CanvasDevAiBuilder controllers drop the available_regions token context accordingly.

The canvas_page_builder_agent and canvas_template_builder_agent system prompts (ai_agents.ai_agent.*.yml) are rewritten to state that content is the only region components can be placed in; canvas_template_builder_agent's description and prompt no longer mention adapting to theme-specific region names, and its YAML output format uses a fixed content key instead of region_name. CanvasAiPageVariantSettingsForm, its route canvas_ai.page_variant_settings, its local task, and the canvas_ai.page_variant.settings config schema are deleted outright.

Three new update functions land in canvas_ai.post_update.php: canvas_ai_post_update_0012_reimport_region_free_builder_agents() re-imports just the system_prompt (and, for the template builder, description) keys of both agents from config/install without disturbing other per-site config, and canvas_ai_post_update_0013_delete_page_variant_settings() deletes canvas_ai.page_variant.settings from every config collection and rebuilds routes. Per the issue's stated scope, the region parameter accepted by the placement tools (PlaceComponents, PlacementOperation, etc.) and validated via CanvasAiPageBuilderHelper::getRegionIndex()/validateRegionExists() is left untouched, deferred to a follow-up issue.

Upgrade

Sites that had customized the canvas_page_builder_agent or canvas_template_builder_agent system prompts directly will have those customizations overwritten by the update hooks; use the Context Control Center or custom event subscribers to alter agent behavior instead. Any values previously entered in the "Page Variant Descriptions" admin form (canvas_ai.page_variant.settings) are deleted and cannot be recovered after update.

item.title: #3592009: Have date props display in the format of the selected locale
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592009 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Canvas stores date, date-time, and time props as raw ISO strings and previously passed them to templates unchanged, leaving component authors to write their own locale formatting. This adds opt-in helpers, canvasFormatDate, canvasFormatDateTime, canvasFormatTime, and canvasFormatDateRange, usable both as Twig filters (in SDC templates) and as JavaScript/TypeScript functions (in code components). They render the value in the site's active Drupal interface language and always treat a value without a UTC offset as UTC, so a stored date never shifts to the previous or next day because of the visitor's local timezone.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New Twig filters canvasFormatDate, canvasFormatDateTime, canvasFormatTime, canvasFormatDateRange and matching JS/TS exports (canvasFormatDate, canvasFormatDateTime, canvasFormatTime, canvasFormatDateRange, type CanvasDateFormatOptions) from drupal-canvas for locale-aware formatting of Canvas date props.

Technical details

On the PHP side, a new Drupal\canvas\Utility\DateResolver service backs the Twig filters registered in CanvasTwigExtension. It reads the current interface language and formats with IntlDateFormatter when the intl extension is available, falling back to PHP date() patterns in the generated, @internal DateFallbackPatterns class (produced by scripts/generate-date-fallback-patterns.php from ICU short-format data) for environments without ext-intl.

On the JS side, date-utils.ts in the drupal-canvas package implements the same four functions using Intl.DateTimeFormat with timeZone: 'UTC', reading the locale from a new drupalSettings.canvasData.v0.langcode value. That setting is a new addition to DrupalSettings and to the allowed dataDependencies.drupalSettings values (canvas.js_component.* schema, ComponentSourceHooks::ASSET_LIBRARY_METHOD_MAPPING, CodeComponentDataProvider::getCanvasDataLangcodeV0); it's populated automatically whenever a code component imports any of the four functions from drupal-canvas, similar to how other v0.* settings are attached on demand.

Upgrade

Component authors can opt in without any migration; existing components keep receiving raw ISO strings unless they use the new helpers.

Twig (SDC) templates:

<p>{{ my_date_prop|canvasFormatDate }}</p>
<p>{{ my_datetime_prop|canvasFormatDateTime }}</p>

Code components (JSX/TSX):

import { canvasFormatDate, canvasFormatDateTime } from 'drupal-canvas';

const formattedDate = canvasFormatDate(myDateProp);
const formattedDateTime = canvasFormatDateTime(myDatetimeProp, { dateStyle: 'long' });

Importing any of the four functions automatically adds v0.langcode to the component's dataDependencies.drupalSettings.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: August 28, 2026

item.title: #3592019: Sync brand kit colors through canvas.brand-kit.json in the Canvas CLI
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592019 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The Canvas CLI can now version brand kit colors the same way it already does fonts. Previously, a project's color palette could only be managed in the Canvas editor UI, so it wasn't tracked in git, reviewable in a merge request, or portable between environments, and offline Workbench previews couldn't render components with the site's real colors. Now canvas.brand-kit.json carries a colors map alongside fonts: canvas pull writes the site's palette into the file, canvas push creates or updates colors on the site to match, and canvas validate checks the file offline (JSON syntax, schema, and semantic rules like duplicate names). Workbench previews now render the local palette from this file even without a site connection. Brand kit sync (fonts and colors) is also switched on by default for pull/push when the file is present, whereas previously fonts had to be opted into explicitly.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Permission change: canvas_oauth's default scope now includes canvas:brand_kit whenever brand kit sync is enabled, and the canvas_oauth authentication provider now allowlists the Color and Folder config entity routes for Bearer-authenticated requests.
  • API change: Brand kit sync (fonts and colors) is now on by default for canvas pull and canvas push when canvas.brand-kit.json exists; --include-brand-kit (positive form) is deprecated in favor of --no-include-brand-kit to opt out.
  • New API: canvas.brand-kit.json gains a colors map (CSS variable key to CSS color string or {value, name, displayFormat} object), synced by canvas pull/canvas push and checked by canvas validate.

Technical details

The file format mirrors a Tailwind theme/W3C design tokens shape: each key becomes a CSS custom property (brand-red maps to --brand-red), map order is palette order, and the display name is derived from the key unless a {value, name, displayFormat} wrapper asserts one. Serialization (packages/cli/src/lib/colors/color-pull.ts) is lossless by construction: serializeColorValue writes a plain CSS string only when it round-trips to the exact same color token, otherwise it falls back to the object form, so a pull immediately after a push produces no diff. color-push.ts matches file entries to server Color entities by CSS variable, only reassigns weights when relative order actually differs (needsWeightReassignment), and only applies a derived name/display format on creation, never renaming a color set in the UI (assertedName). Push is non-destructive by default: server-only colors are reported via serverOnly, and the new --prune-colors flag opts into deletion, with in-use colors reported and failing the command at the end rather than aborting mid-run. Offline validation (color-validate.ts) mirrors the server's unique-name constraint (trimmed, case-insensitive) before any request is made.

Component color props that reference a brand kit color use a canvas-color:<key> example value; pull rewrites the server's canvas-color:<uuid> form to the file's canvas-color:<cssVarKey> form, and push does the reverse when serializing components, matching by the cssVariable the discovery layer resolves.

Server-side, CanvasOauthAuthenticationProvider now allowlists Color::ENTITY_TYPE_ID and Folder::ENTITY_TYPE_ID routes so Bearer-authenticated CLI requests can reach the color config entity endpoints, and openapi.yml documents BrandKit.colors as a read-only, derived list (colors are managed through the dedicated color endpoints, not by writing BrandKit.colors directly). Enabling brand kit sync now also adds canvas:brand_kit to the default OAuth scope automatically (packages/cli/src/config.ts).</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">Brand kit sync (fonts and colors) is now on by default whenever canvas.brand-kit.json exists. To keep the previous opt-in behavior, disable it explicitly:

npx canvas pull --no-include-brand-kit
npx canvas push --no-include-brand-kit
# or
CANVAS_INCLUDE_BRAND_KIT=false

The positive --include-brand-kit flag is deprecated (it still works but emits a warning); scripts that used it to opt in no longer need it. Existing OAuth tokens will pick up the new canvas:brand_kit scope on their next refresh.

To add colors to a project's canvas.brand-kit.json:

{
  "colors": {
    "brand-red": "#cc0000",
    "overlay": "hsla(220, 60%, 50%, 0.5)",
    "accent": { "value": "#0000cc", "name": "Accent blue" }
  }
}

Run npx canvas pull to populate it from the site, or npx canvas push to send local entries; add --prune-colors to also delete site colors absent from the file (colors currently in use by a component or template are reported and left in place).</upgrade> <parameter name="collaboration">

item.title: #3591996: RecipeAppliedEvent listener installs a module and invalidates the container for every listener after it
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591996 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

Applying a Drupal CMS style "Site" recipe that enables Canvas together with a theme that defines page regions could crash the site installation with a fatal error: "You have requested a synthetic service ("kernel"). The DIC does not know how to construct this service." This happened because Canvas's recipe listener installed a helper module mid dispatch, which rebuilt Drupal's service container while other modules' recipe listeners (for example drupal_cms_helper's, which saves system.site config) were still queued to run against the old, now stale container. The fix reorders Canvas's internal recipe handling so the step that can trigger a module install, and therefore a container rebuild, always runs last. Site owners installing Drupal CMS or any Site type recipe alongside Canvas no longer hit this installation failure.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

RecipeSubscriber::getSubscribedEvents() previously mapped RecipeAppliedEvent to a single onApply() method that, for Site type recipes, called PageVariantMigration::migrateDefaultTheme() inline. That method's createFromPageRegions() conditionally installs canvas_page_template_component via ModuleInstallerInterface::install() when missing, and InstallerKernel::attachSynthetic() calls $this->container?->reset() on every install to bound memory growth. Any RecipeAppliedEvent listener still queued behind Canvas's, holding a reference to the pre-reset container (including synthetic services like @kernel, which Canvas's own ComponentSourceManager depends on), would then fail to resolve.

The fix splits the event registration into two listeners: the original onApply() (unchanged, re-runs config actions targeting Component entities) and a new static migrateSiteTemplate() registered at priority PHP_INT_MIN in RecipeSubscriber::getSubscribedEvents(), guaranteeing it runs after every other RecipeAppliedEvent subscriber, including third-party ones such as drupal_cms_helper's. migrateSiteTemplate() performs the same PageVariantMigration::migrateDefaultTheme() call for Site recipes, but since it now runs last, the container rebuild triggered by installing canvas_page_template_component can no longer invalidate a container that other listeners still need.

item.title: #3591934: Add component label to settings form
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591934 · 1 contributor · 8 comments

Summary

In Drupal Canvas's editing UI, the settings panel used to edit a selected component's props did not show which component it belonged to. If the selection changed unexpectedly, such as when the canvas scrolled or the UI lagged after a quick action, it was easy to lose track of what you were actually editing. The settings form now displays the component's name in bold at the top of the panel, so it is always clear which component's settings are being edited.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The fix is in ComponentInstanceFormRenderer (ui/src/components/ComponentInstanceForm.tsx). It derives selectedComponentName from components?.[selectedComponentType]?.name and, when non-empty, renders it in a bold Text inside a Box immediately above the TransformsContext.Provider that wraps the generated JSX props form. A corresponding Cypress test asserts that the element with data-testid="selected-component-name" shows the expected label (e.g. 'All props') when that test component's form is open.

item.title: #3591860: Add a button to close the right tray
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591860 · 1 contributor · 4 comments
  • Followers: 1

Summary

The Canvas Editor's right-hand contextual panel (used for component settings, crop controls, and prop editing) previously stayed open once populated, taking up screen space even when its content wasn't needed. This adds a close ("X") icon to the panel so editors can manually hide it and get more room for the canvas. item.title: #3592032: Canvas AI: Proper chat history management in the backend
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592032 · 1 contributor · 50 comments

Summary

The Canvas dev AI chat (an experimental page-builder assistant, part of the canvas_dev_ai module) used to forget everything it had done as soon as a chat turn finished. Each new message started the agent from scratch, so it would re-read component schemas and redo lookups it had already performed earlier in the same conversation, wasting extra round trips. This change lets the backend keep the agent's own history, including its tool calls and their results, across turns within the same chat session, so follow-up requests can skip work already done. Because keeping this history costs more tokens per request, it is off by default and must be turned on explicitly via a new checkbox on the Agents & Tools configuration form.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: New keep_tool_calls_in_history boolean added to canvas_dev_ai.settings (default FALSE), togglable on the Canvas AI Agents & Tools form at /admin/config/ai/canvas-ai-agent-selection.

The frontend (AiWizardDev.tsx) now generates one conversation_id per mount of the chat panel (the chat is cleared on mount) and sends it with every turn, alongside the existing per-turn request_id. On the backend, CanvasDevAiBuilder no longer unconditionally deletes the stored agent state when a turn finishes: if keep_tool_calls_in_history is enabled, it calls the new CanvasAiTempStore::setStoredConversationState() to persist the finished agent's serialized state (via ::toArray()) keyed by conversation_id and tagged with the agent_id that produced it. On the next turn, prepareAgent() looks up that stored conversation state and, if it exists and belongs to the same agent, resumes it with $agent->fromArray() instead of rebuilding history from the client transcript via CanvasAiChatHelper::getFilteredChatHistory(). The resumed state's looped counter is reset to 0 so the new user message is appended and the per-turn loop ceiling still applies. If a turn ends unsolvable (the agent gave up or errored), forgetTurn() deletes both the per-turn agent state and the conversation state, so the following turn falls back to seeding from the transcript rather than resuming a broken history. item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas

This happened when a shared cache or CDN sat in front of the site's content API: it didn't distinguish between an anonymous published request and an authenticated preview request carrying a draft token, so it could serve the cached published response to the editor's preview. Canvas's content API responses now vary caching by the request's authorization credentials, so shared caches treat preview requests separately from published ones and editors reliably see their draft content.

item.title: #3592062: Support rendering SVGs in SDC and code components with an image prop
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592062 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Canvas (Experience Builder) lets editors place an SVG media item into a component's image prop, but until now the SVG silently failed to render: the image was requested through a resizing/derivative pipeline that cannot process SVGs, producing broken image requests, and the unknown width/height of an unprocessable image was recorded as 0 rather than "unknown", which makes an <img> invisible. A third, related bug made the Image wrapper used by code components always assume a resizing loader was available, logging an error for every candidate size on an SVG. With this fix, SVGs assigned to an image prop (in SDCs and code components) render correctly, sized from the SVG's own width/height or viewBox when available. SVG support remains opt-in per media type; Canvas' default allowed file extensions are unchanged.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Evaluator no longer casts a NULL-resolving primitive prop value to 0, '', or false; an optional object prop with no value is now omitted/absent (visible in inputs_resolved and in code component props) instead of a false-y placeholder, and empty items in a multiple-cardinality static prop preview are omitted instead of becoming 0. Required props are unaffected since they still map onto required field properties that throw when empty.

Technical details

The fix targets three call sites that assumed every image file could be resized. ImageDerivativeWithParametrizedWidth and ComputedUrlWithQueryString (and ImageAndStyleAdapter) now check ImageStyle::supportsUri() before building a canvas_parametrized_width--{width} derivative URL or appending an ?alternateWidths= query string, and omit the query parameter entirely when it would evaluate to NULL, so srcset candidates are no longer generated for files the image toolkit can't process.

Separately, Evaluator stopped casting NULL-resolving primitive field property values with (int)/(string)/(bool), which previously turned an unreadable image's width/height into 0. Object props that evaluate to NULL are now omitted rather than serialized as a false-y value, since null doesn't validate against most prop shapes. This uncovered two related bugs that were also fixed: access-denied inference for a required-but-empty field property had assumed Typed Data marks width/height as required (it doesn't), and a computed field property that resolves to NULL still needs to carry cacheability from the property definition rather than from the (absent) computed value. At save time, SVG intrinsic dimensions are now read from the SVG's own width/height attributes (when in pixels) or its viewBox, so an icon without explicit width/height doesn't get stretched to fill its containing block.

The Image wrapper for code components (built on next-image-standalone) now marks an image unoptimized when there's no alternateWidths to build a loader from, which omits srcset/sizes instead of invoking a loader that assumes optimization always applies.

Upgrade

Code that reads inputs_resolved or code component props for an optional image-shaped prop should no longer expect a 0, '', or false placeholder when the value is absent or unresolvable; such props are now simply omitted. Required props are unaffected. See the change record at #3623307 for details.

item.title: #3592000: Translating a component tree config entity (such as PageVariant) that has an auto-save draft breaks Canvas layout validation
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592000 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

If a PageVariant or ContentTemplate had unpublished changes sitting in Canvas's auto-save draft when it was translated via config translation, the next time anyone opened the Canvas editor it would crash with a 500 error on every layout request, and stay crashed since the error masked the whole screen (there was no way to publish or discard the draft to recover). This affected plain, single-language-default sites, not just multilingual ones with langcode drift. The fix stops this crash: translating an entity that has a pending auto-save draft no longer breaks the editor.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The crash came from CanvasConfigEntityTranslationsAreValidConstraintValidator::validate(), which simulates Config::setOverriddenData() by running NestedArray::mergeDeepArray() on the entity's base component_tree and the LanguageConfigOverride's translated data, then validates the merged array against config schema. A saved component_tree is re-keyed by instance UUID in ComponentTreeConfigEntityBase::preSave(), but an auto-save draft never runs preSave(), so a draft created before the translation existed keeps the client's delta keys (0, 1, 2, …). A LanguageConfigOverride, however, always targets instances by UUID. Merging a delta-keyed base with a UUID-keyed override made the merge treat them as disjoint sets, appending the override's sparse translated inputs as a phantom component instance with no component_id, component_version, or uuid. Validating that merged data tripped the assert(\array_key_exists('component_id', $component_instance)) in ComponentInputsMapping::__construct().

The fix re-keys the base component_tree by UUID before the merge, calling ComponentTreeConfigEntityBase::asDeterministicallyAndTranslatableKeyedComponentTreeSequence(), mirroring what getTranslatedComponentTree() already did for a different code path (as noted in that method's own docblock). Test coverage was added in PageVariantValidationTest::testValidationWithTranslationOverrideAndDeltaKeyedTree, which reconstructs the delta-keyed draft shape, adds a UUID-targeted hu override, and asserts no validation errors. This fix was split out of the broader langcode-drift work in #3591850 (MR !1400) because it reproduces under plain, single-language-default conditions.

No action needed for typical Canvas usage; this is an internal bug fix. For context: ComponentTreeConfigEntityBase::asDeterministicallyAndTranslatableKeyedComponentTreeSequence() was changed from private to public (and marked @internal) so the validator could reuse the same re-keying logic. Canvas Code Components are described by an authored component.yml file, but until now the rules for what counts as valid metadata were scattered across the CLI, JSON Schema prop definitions, Drupal config schema, and PHP entity constraints. That made local feedback incomplete and meant errors could surface only partway through a canvas push, after other components had already been updated. Summary

Canvas's code editor previously recognized only "Image" and "Video" object prop types. A code component prop using the newly added document schema shape ($ref to canvas.module/document) would silently vanish from the Props panel, and there was no way to add a new document prop from the UI.
